summary: This figure from BFMSense's case study on respiration monitoring explains why sensing quality depends on a target's initial position. Panel (a) plots the beamforming feedback matrix (BFM) signal's trajectory on the complex plane for a 'Good position' (gold dashed arc) versus a 'Bad position' (grey solid arc): the good-position trajectory sweeps a longer arc of the underlying circle, while the bad-position one covers only a short, nearly straight fragment. Panels (b) and (c) show the corresponding BFM amplitude and phase waveforms over time, each split into a top row (good position, large oscillations) and bottom row (bad position, small, noise-prone oscillations). The figure argues that respiration-induced BFM variation is only a fragment of a full rotation, so its size, and therefore how easily it can be detected, depends on where along the circle that fragment falls.
